mechanism_landscape.target: EGFR / BRAF / ALK targeted protein degradation (TPD)
mechanism_landscape.drug_class: PROTAC degraders + molecular glues (EGFR, BRAF, ALK, GSPT1)
mechanism_landscape.leading_pipeline_asset: CFT8919 (EGFR degrader, C797S-active); HSK40118 / ONPR-04 (China EGFR PROTACs); CFT1946 (BRAF V600 PROTAC basket); MRT-2359 (GSPT1 glue); CM-701/CM-486 (ALK glues, preclinical)
mechanism_landscape.key_resistance_mechanism: Differentiation thesis (preclinical): degraders' catalytic mode means residual ligand affinity is sufficient to drive degradation even against occupancy-resistance mutants (EGFR C797S, T790M+C797S double mutant, ALK G1202R/L1196M) that escape occupancy-based inhibitors; degradation also ablates kinase-independent scaffolding functions. Read-across to BTK-PROTAC vs ibrutinib-resistant BTK-C481S precedent. Compound EGFR mutations remain 'particularly difficult to treat' — degraders are 'a logical next step' but superiority vs next-gen inhibitors 'remains an open question'. China dominates clinical-stage EGFR-PROTAC pipeline. No Ph1 readouts vs osimertinib-failed patients yet. Sources: Nat Rev Drug Discov kinase-modulator review (DOI 10.1038/s41573-026-01411-9); Nat Rev Cancer TPD review (DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00817-8)

mechanism_landscape.drug_class: STING agonists ± hypomethylating agents; downstream IRF3-IFN-I strategies
mechanism_landscape.key_resistance_mechanism: Mechanistic framing (no clinical-stage NSCLC asset named): (1) STING promoter hypermethylation (DNMT1/EZH2-driven) occurs in dormant lung-adeno tumour cells and accelerates metastatic outbreak; STING agonists alone eliminate dormant metastases T-/NK-cell-dependently — rationale for STING-agonist + hypomethylating-agent combo in post-resection adjuvant / MRD-positive NSCLC. (2) Recurrent STING loss in lung adenocarcinoma is a structural barrier to STING-agonist monotherapy, supporting demethylation, tumour-targeted ADC delivery, or downstream IRF3-IFN-I targeting. (3) ERCC1-deficient NSCLC accumulates cytosolic dsDNA and engages cGAS-STING — candidate STING-engagement stratification biomarker (ERCC1 IHC not yet routine). Source: Lu C, Wang W, Fu Y-X. Nat Rev Cancer 26, 200-216 (2026); DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00894-9, p.205-209

mechanism_landscape.drug_class: Personalised neoantigen mRNA + shared-antigen mRNA + peptide/DC vaccines (± checkpoint blockade)
mechanism_landscape.leading_pipeline_asset: intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157, Moderna/Merck, Ph3 adjuvant NCT06077760); BNT116 (BioNTech, shared-antigen Ph1 NCT05142189)
mechanism_landscape.key_resistance_mechanism: Framing: NSCLC is the #2 indication for therapeutic cancer vaccines after melanoma — ~two dozen NSCLC-directed therapeutic cancer-vaccine agents in active clinical development (inclusion: Ph1–3; DC / peptide / mRNA / viral-vector platforms; NSCLC named as a target indication, incl. pan-tumor baskets with an NSCLC cohort; EXCLUDES preclinical-only and discontinued programs) per WS13 cancer-vaccine + mRNA reviews (2026) — landscape-density estimate, not enumerated in-draft; the ETLM profiles the lead agents (intismeran Ph3, BNT116 Ph1) individually. Platform diversity reflects high-TMB neoantigen feasibility plus shared-TAA (MUC1, viral antigens) optionality. Central open question: whether NSCLC has sufficient neoantigen diversity to favour personalised (intismeran) over shared (BNT116) approaches — lower TMB in non-smokers is a concern. No Phase III NSCLC vaccine readout yet anchors the field; checkpoint-combination is the dominant clinical hypothesis carried from melanoma's mRNA-4157 validation. Sources: Nat Rev Drug Discov cancer-vaccine landscape (DOI 10.1038/d41573-026-00063-z), p.5; mRNA-therapeutics review (DOI 10.1038/s41573-026-01459-7)

unmet_needs.need: ILD risk-management for DXd / TOPO1-payload ADCs in NSCLC — interstitial lung disease is now understood as a payload-class effect, not a HER2-specific issue
unmet_needs.patient_fraction: All NSCLC patients receiving DXd-payload ADCs (TROP2, HER3, HER2)
unmet_needs.leading_approaches: Per Zippelius A et al. Nat Rev Cancer 25, 925-944 (2025; DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00869-w): ILD originally seen with anti-HER2 ADCs (T-DM1, T-DXd) now appears across DXd-family TOPO1-payload ADCs regardless of target — datopotamab deruxtecan (TROP2) and patritumab deruxtecan (HER3) both show ILD signals. Mechanism: high payload retention on alveolar macrophages via FcgammaR uptake + low baseline antigen on respiratory epithelium. Any next-gen DXd-payload ADC entering NSCLC needs an upfront ILD risk-management strategy

unmet_needs.need: Differentiation in the crowded TOPO1-payload ADC field in NSCLC — TROP2 (Dato-DXd, sac-TMT, sacituzumab govitecan), HER3 (patritumab DXd) and follow-on TOPO1 ADCs converge on the same population
unmet_needs.leading_approaches: Per Zippelius 2025 review: differentiation must come from biomarker selection (TROP2 IHC, HER3 expression), linker/payload tuning, or ADC-ICI combination architecture rather than target novelty. ADC-ICI synergy looks most promising in NSCLC (with mTNBC) — EVOKE-02 Cohort A (sac-govitecan + pembro, 1L PD-L1≥50%) and TROPION-Lung02 subgroup (dato-DXd + pembro ± chemo) are lead non-randomised signals; 1L mNSCLC is the next likely ADC-ICI battleground after urothelial

unmet_needs.need: c-MET ADC tolerability gap in NSCLC — MMAE-payload cMET ADCs carry ocular toxicity vs cleaner DXd-payload ADCs
unmet_needs.patient_fraction: MET-overexpressing / MET-altered NSCLC receiving cMET ADCs
unmet_needs.leading_approaches: Per Zippelius 2025 review: ocular toxicity has discontinued several site-specific MMAE conjugates; telisotuzumab vedotin and MYTX-011 (both MMAE-based cMET ADCs) exemplify the tolerability gap vs DXd-payload ADCs

competitive_dynamics.evoke03_halt_note: Trodelvy EVOKE-03 (sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab) Phase 3 halted June 2026 in 1L PD-L1-high NSCLC — primary endpoint not met. Removes sacituzumab govitecan (SG-ADC, Gilead/Merck) as a competitive entrant in 1L IO-combination space. Opens 1L PD-L1-high ADC combination space for Daiichi/AZ dato-DXd, sac-TMT (MK-2870), and future TROP2-IO programs. Source: event_ids 194/196/199 (priority 0.85-0.93), 2026-06-09
competitive_dynamics.gsk_nuvalent_acquisition_note: GSK $10.6B acquisition of Nuvalent (announced 2026-06-09) — brings zidesamtinib (ROS1 3rd-gen, ARROS-1) and neladalkib (ALK 4th-gen, ALKOVE-1) NDA-stage precision NSCLC assets into Top-5 pharma. PDUFA decisions expected 2026. Reshapes ROS1 commercial (currently Pfizer crizotinib/lorlatinib + BMS repotrectinib) and post-lorlatinib ALK resistance (currently white-space). Acquisition premium ~30% over Nuvalent equity; establishes precedent for late-stage precision-oncology biotech acqui-hire pricing. Source: KB events 192/195/197 (priority 0.97-0.98), 2026-06-09
competitive_dynamics.adc_ici_combination_note: Review-derived framing (Zippelius A et al. Nat Rev Cancer 25, 925-944, 2025; DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00869-w): NSCLC is one of two indications (with mTNBC) where ADC-ICI synergy looks most promising. Lead non-randomised signals: sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab in 1L PD-L1≥50% mNSCLC (EVOKE-02 Cohort A) and datopotamab deruxtecan + pembrolizumab ± platinum in 1L aNSCLC (TROPION-Lung02 subgroup). Randomised confirmation ongoing; 1L mNSCLC is the next likely ADC-ICI battleground after urothelial. NB EVOKE-02 (1L combination signal) is distinct from EVOKE-03 (sac-govitecan + pembro 1L PD-L1-high Ph3, halted June 2026 — see evoke03_halt_note). Review also reframes the NSCLC ADC field as a converging TOPO1-payload crowd (TROP2 + HER3) where differentiation comes from biomarker selection, linker/payload tuning, or ADC-ICI architecture, not target novelty
competitive_dynamics.vaccine_pipeline_density_note: ~24 NSCLC-targeted therapeutic cancer-vaccine agents across DC / peptide / mRNA platforms — second-most-pursued vaccine indication after melanoma. Platform diversity reflects TMB-driven neoantigen feasibility plus shared-TAA (MUC1, viral) optionality. Personalised-vs-shared mRNA fork in NSCLC: intismeran autogene (Moderna/Merck, personalised, Ph3 NCT06077760) vs BNT116 (BioNTech, 6 shared antigens, Ph1 NCT05142189). Sources: Nat Rev Drug Discov cancer-vaccine landscape (DOI 10.1038/d41573-026-00063-z), p.5; mRNA-therapeutics review (DOI 10.1038/s41573-026-01459-7)
competitive_dynamics.jak_io_potentiation_note: Emerging non-cytotoxic ICB-combination axis in NSCLC: JAK1-selective inhibitor + PD-1 blockade. itacitinib + pembrolizumab Ph2 in treatment-naive NSCLC reported mPFS 23.8 mo / RR 67%. Mechanistic rationale (cGAS-STING + JAK-STAT reviews): chronic IFN-I responsiveness in patient T cells correlates with inferior survival; JAK inhibition dampens this and reduces CD8+ exhaustion, potentiating PD-1 — explains JAK-monotherapy failures vs JAK+IO signal. Distinct from dominant chemo-ICB and ADC-ICI paradigms. China sponsor signal: golidocitinib (Dizal, JAK1i, first-in-class in China r/r PTCL, Ph2 NSCLC). danvatirsen (Flamingo, STAT3 ASO) adds antisense modality. Sources: Nat Rev Drug Discov JAK-STAT review (DOI 10.1038/s41573-025-01336-9), p.282; Nat Rev Cancer cGAS-STING review (DOI 10.1038/s41568-025-00894-9), p.209
competitive_dynamics.egfr_resistance_frontier_note: Compound EGFR mutations (T790M+C797S, exon-20 insertions, exon19del+C797S) remain 'particularly difficult to treat' with kinase inhibitors. Multiple groups pursuing degrader strategies (CFT8919, HSK40118, ONPR-04); whether degraders achieve superior efficacy/durability vs next-gen inhibitors 'remains an open question' but represents 'a logical next step in overcoming therapeutic resistance in EGFR-driven malignancies'. China dominates the clinical-stage EGFR-PROTAC pipeline. Source: Rudolph J et al. Nat Rev Drug Discov 2026 (DOI 10.1038/s41573-026-01411-9), 'BRAF and EGFR'
